=== .dwe/config ===
# .dwe/config — per-project DWE user overrides (gitignored, all-commented).
#
# This file pins per-developer preferences for THIS project without touching the
# global ~/.config/dwe/config. It is read by every `dwe` invocation run inside
# the project and is layered: global config < this file < environment variables.
#
# Syntax: flat `key = value` lines. Full-line `#` comments only (an inline `#`
# after a space is a parse error). Booleans accept 1/true/yes and 0/false/no.
# Unknown keys are warnings, not errors. Uncomment a line to activate it.
#
# Every key below is shown with its default. Run `dwe docs show config/userconfig`
# for the authoritative reference.

# --- Locale and TUI ---
# Preferred locale for translated strings. Unset → $LANG → en.
# language = en
# Mermaid theme for the `dwe docs` TUI: auto | dark | light. Default: auto.
# mermaid_theme = auto

# --- Binary overrides ---
# Absolute path DWE uses when invoking each external binary. Empty is rejected.
# binary_docker = docker
# binary_git    = git
# binary_dwe    = dwe
# binary_shell  = sh
# binary_mmdc   = mmdc

# --- Notifications ---
# Master gate for desktop notifications. Default: false.
# notify_enabled          = false
# Per-surface gates (only consulted when notify_enabled is true).
# notify_deploy_enabled   = true
# notify_run_enabled      = true
# notify_commands_enabled = true
# Comma-separated channel list (e.g. native).
# notify_channels         = native

=== AGENTS.md ===
# myproj — DWE project

This repository is a **DWE** (Dev Workspace Engine) project: a Docker-based local
development environment managed by the `dwe` CLI.

## Orientation for AI agents

Run this once to load a project-aware index of services, commands, and docs:

```
dwe docs llms-txt --lang en
```

It emits a compact llms.txt briefing (project context, services, commands, the
pipeline builtin inventory, the diagnostic flags, the template-syntax map, and
pointers into the built-in docs subsystem) designed to be loaded once and then
navigated on demand. The generic part stays under 12 KB; read it in full rather
than grepping it.

## Conventions for AI agents

- **Docs in English.** Pass `--lang en` to every `dwe docs …` command (`llms-txt`,
  `show`, `search`, `list`) — translated docs can lag behind the English source.
- **Data as JSON.** For any command whose output you parse — `dwe status`,
  `dwe validate`, `dwe info`, `dwe services list`, `dwe commands list`,
  `dwe docs list`, `dwe docs search`, `dwe vars …` — add `--output json`
  (alias `-o json`); the default table output is formatted for humans.
  **Exception:** `dwe docs llms-txt` and `dwe docs show` always emit markdown and
  ignore `-o json` — the document itself is the payload. To write `llms-txt` to a
  file use that command's own `--out PATH` flag.

## Useful commands

Day-to-day work goes through the first two — they cover most of what an agent needs:

- `dwe commands list` — list this project's declared dev commands (tests, linters,
  migrations, …); `dwe cmd <id>` runs one, `dwe cmd -i <id>` shows its definition
  (type, service, workdir, the underlying command, its params)
- `dwe shell <service> -c '<cmd>'` — run a one-off command inside a service
  container, for anything not covered by a declared command

Inspecting the environment:

- `dwe` — project dashboard / header
- `dwe status` — stack health, per-service state and container names
- `dwe info` — environment summary (URLs, hosts, ports)
- `dwe logs [service]` — stream container logs
- `dwe validate` — static project-config validation

Lifecycle and reference:

- `dwe deploy run` — run the deploy pipeline (first-time provisioning, image
  builds, migrations); `dwe run` starts an already-provisioned stack
- `dwe docs show <topic> --lang en` — built-in reference (config schemas, guides);
  `dwe docs list --lang en` enumerates topics, `dwe docs search <substring> --lang en`
  searches them

## Config layout

- `workspace.yml` — project identity (name, prefix)
- `workspace/defaults.yml` — versioned defaults (service toggles, exports, `vars:`)
- `workspace/styles.yml` — CLI branding and palette
- `workspace/services/<name>/service.yml` — per-service definitions; the folder
  name **is** the service key (there is no `name:` field)
- `workspace/services/<name>/deploy.yml` — that service's provisioning pipeline
- `workspace/templates/{config,ide,ai,git}/` — render packs
- `workspace/tests/<scenario>.yml` — isolated integration-test scenarios
  (`dwe test list`, `dwe validate tests`)
- `workspace/{deploy,lifecycle,info}.yml` — optional pipeline overrides. They ship
  fully commented; the built-in defaults stay active until you uncomment, and an
  active section **replaces** the whole built-in one — copy every phase you still
  want, don't uncomment a fragment.
- `workspace/docker.yml` — compose policy. Unlike the pipelines above, overriding
  here is **per key**: an uncommented key replaces just that key's default.

## The two `AGENTS.md` files

- **This file** (project root) is scaffolded once by `dwe init` and then
  hand-maintained. Edit it — it is where project-specific facts belong.
- A service hub (`services/<name>/`) gets a **generated** `AGENTS.md` from the
  `ai` render pack. `dwe render ai` writes it. With **no service argument** it
  walks every service and honours each `render.ai.enabled`, so one step covers
  the whole project. Refreshing on deploy is opt-in — the built-in default
  pipeline has no render phase. To wire it up, uncomment `workspace/deploy.yml`
  and add a single `type: dwe`, `cmd: "render ai"` step there; do **not** add a
  per-service `render ai <name>` step to each `services/<name>/deploy.yml`.
  Never edit the generated file; edit `workspace/templates/ai/<pack>/` instead.
  It appears only after the hub directory exists (i.e. after the first clone).

> `CLAUDE.md` next to this file is a symlink to it (a copy on platforms without
> symlinks). Edit `AGENTS.md`.

--------
=== compose.yaml ===
# Base compose file for this DWE project.
#
# DWE merges this base with per-service compose overlays it generates from
# workspace/services/<name>/service.yml. Add project-wide compose configuration
# here (named volumes, networks, shared settings); per-service containers are
# managed by DWE and normally do not need a hand-written entry.
#
# Referenced from workspace/defaults.yml as `compose.base: compose.yaml`.

--------
=== workspace.yml ===
# workspace.yml — structural identity for this DWE project (layer 1 of 3).
#
# This is the only required project file. workspace/defaults.yml (layer 2) and
# workspace/local.yml (layer 3, gitignored) layer on top of it; keys absent here
# fall through to those layers. Run `dwe docs show config/workspace` for the full
# merge model.

project:
  name: "myproj"
  prefix: "dwe"

--------
=== workspace/defaults.yml ===
# workspace/defaults.yml — versioned project defaults (layer 2 of 3).
#
# Tracked by git. Everything here is overridable per-developer in
# workspace/local.yml (gitignored). Run `dwe docs show config/workspace`.

# Compose base file (always included by the Docker control plane).
compose:
  base: compose.yaml

# Service toggles. Service definitions live in
# workspace/services/<name>/service.yml; this overlay only flips enabled state
# (allowed keys per entry: enabled, ports, hosts).
services:
  "app":
    enabled: true

# runtime:
#   use_https: false
#   spx:
#     path: ""

# state: ""

# Declarative .env export rules. Each rule maps a dot-path in the merged config
# to an environment variable. See `dwe docs show config/workspace`.
#
# This is the second half of the port pair: a port declared in
# workspace/services/<name>/service.yml is display-only until a rule here
# exports it, so compose.yaml can bind it. Uncomment both together.
# PROJECT, UID and GID are injected automatically and must not be redeclared.
# exports:
#   env:
#     - name: APP_PORT
#       from: services.<name>.ports.http
#       format: int

=== workspace/deploy.yml ===
# workspace/deploy.yml — project deploy pipeline (INERT MIRROR).
#
# The built-in default deploy pipeline is ACTIVE. This file is shipped fully
# commented so the default keeps running untouched. Uncomment to override —
# doing so REPLACES the whole pipeline (composition is full-replacement, not a
# merge), so copy every phase you still want, then edit.
#
# Authoritative default: deploy.DefaultDeployConfig()
#   (internal/core/workflow/deploy/defaults.go)
# Schema and field reference: `dwe docs show config/deploy/index`
#
# log: true
# phases:
#   - name: services
#     description: "Deploy all enabled services (resolved by dependency order)"
#     deploy_services: true
#   - name: start
#     description: "Start containers and wait for health"
#     steps:
#       - name: up
#         type: dwe
#         cmd: "docker up --wait"
#         description: "Start all containers and wait until healthy"
#         untracked: true
#   - name: post-deploy
#     description: "Post-deploy summary (runs only if all prior phases succeeded)"
#     untracked: true
#     steps:
#       - name: info
#         type: dwe
#         cmd: "info"
#         description: "Show environment summary"
#       - name: success
#         type: builtin
#         cmd: message
#         with:
#           level: success
#           text: "Deploy completed successfully"

--------
=== workspace/docker.yml ===
# workspace/docker.yml — Docker Compose execution policy (INERT MIRROR).
#
# This file controls how `dwe docker` builds and runs `docker compose` commands
# (project name, per-subcommand args, process env). It is shipped fully
# commented; with no docker.yml the built-in policy applies. Overriding is
# per-key, not whole-file: uncommenting one key replaces only that key, and
# every key you leave commented keeps its built-in default (up, logs, run and
# down carry defaults; the other args keys default to empty).
#
# Per-developer overrides go in workspace/docker.local.yml (gitignored), which
# is deep-merged on top of this file.
# Schema and field reference: `dwe docs show config/docker`
#
# project_name: "${project.prefix}-${project.name}"
#
# args:
#   global: ["--ansi", "always", "--progress", "tty"]
#   up: ["-d", "--remove-orphans"]
#   down: ["--remove-orphans"]
#   logs: ["-f"]
#   run: ["--rm"]
#   pull: []
#   build: []
#
# process_env:
#   DOCKER_CLI_HINTS: "false"

# workspace/info.yml — `dwe info` dashboard (INERT MIRROR).
#
# When this file is absent the built-in default dashboard is rendered. This file
# is shipped fully commented so that default stays active. Uncomment to take
# full control of the dashboard layout — an active info.yml replaces the
# built-in dashboard entirely.
#
# Authoritative behavior: the built-in `dwe info` fallback dashboard.
# Schema, item types, and template expressions: `dwe docs show config/info`

# sections:

=== workspace/lifecycle.yml ===
# workspace/lifecycle.yml — run / stop pipelines (INERT MIRROR).
#
# The built-in default run and stop pipelines are ACTIVE. This file is shipped
# fully commented so the defaults keep running untouched. Uncomment a section to
# override it — each section (run, stop) is full-replacement, not a merge, so
# copy every phase you still want, then edit. (The stop pipeline always has an
# auto-reap phase prepended by the engine regardless of what you author here.)
#
# Authoritative defaults: lifecycle.DefaultRunConfig() / DefaultStopConfig()
#   (internal/core/workflow/lifecycle/defaults.go)
# Schema and field reference: `dwe docs show config/lifecycle`
#
# The self-update probe is NOT configured here — it moved to the top-level
# `update:` block (workspace.yml / local.yml). See
# `dwe docs show config/workspace` § "The update: block".
#
# run:
#   show_info: true
#   final_message: "Project is ready for work!"
#   phases:
#     - name: start
#       description: "Start containers and wait for health"
#       steps:
#         - name: up
#           type: dwe
#           cmd: "docker up --wait"
#           description: "Start all containers and wait until healthy"
#
# stop:
#   final_message: "Project is stopped. Have a nice day!"
#   phases:
#     - name: stop
#       description: "Stop containers"
#       steps:
#         - name: down
#           type: dwe
#           cmd: "docker down"
#           description: "Stop all containers"

--------
=== workspace/services/app/deploy.yml ===
# workspace/services/app/deploy.yml — per-service deploy pipeline (INERT MIRROR).
#
# Inlined by the orchestrator wherever workspace/deploy.yml declares a
# `deploy_services: true` phase (the built-in default does). A service without
# this file is silently skipped, so the whole skeleton below is shipped
# commented and nothing runs until you uncomment it.
#
# The phase shape is the one every DWE app service converges on:
#
#   source     — materialise the hub (clone once, never touch it again)
#   image      — build the container image
#   bootstrap  — first-run setup inside the container
#
# Hub-level artefacts (agent docs, IDE config) are deliberately absent: they
# belong in the PROJECT pipeline, not here. `dwe render ai` with no service
# argument walks every service and honours each `render.ai.enabled`, so one
# step in workspace/deploy.yml keeps every hub up to date and needs no edit
# when services come and go. A per-service `render ai app` step just
# repeats that work. Rendering stays opt-in — the built-in default pipeline has
# no render phase. To wire it up, uncomment workspace/deploy.yml (which replaces
# the whole built-in pipeline — copy every phase you still want) and add there:
#
#     - name: render
#       description: "Render hub-level artefacts"
#       steps:
#         - name: agent-docs
#           type: dwe
#           cmd: "render ai"
#           description: "Render AGENTS.md into every service hub"
#
# Schema and field reference: `dwe docs show config/deploy/index`
# Builtin inventory (name, kind, purpose): `dwe docs llms-txt --lang en`
#
# phases:
#   - name: source
#     description: "Materialise the source hub"
#     steps:
#       - name: clone
#         type: builtin
#         cmd: source_clone
#         description: "Clone the application source into the hub"
#         with:
#           # `repo` usually comes from vars: (`vars.app.repo` in
#           # workspace.yml), so a fork can be pointed at in local.yml.
#           repo: "git@example.com:acme/app.git"
#           dir: "services/app/src"
#           # branch: main
#
#   - name: image
#     description: "Build the service image"
#     steps:
#       - name: build
#         type: dwe
#         cmd: "docker build app"
#         description: "Build the app image"
#
#   - name: bootstrap
#     description: "First-run setup inside the container"
#     steps:
#       - name: deps
#         # Once the project declares this as a user command, dispatch it with
#         # `type: command` + `cmd: <id>` instead — one definition, and the
#         # command carries the service/workdir/user/env. Never paste the bare
#         # `docker compose …` line into a `type: shell` step: it runs on the
#         # HOST, bypasses dwe's -p/-f chain (so it lands in a different compose
#         # project and misses the service's overlays), and every host step
#         # counts against the `host_steps` gate on unattended `dwe test run`.
#         type: dwe
#         cmd: "docker run --rm app -- npm ci"
#         description: "Install dependencies on first deploy"
#         # `check: auto` derives the post-condition from `when:` by negating
#         # it: run while the marker is missing, then assert it now exists.
#         # It is only valid together with a `when:` of type shell — which is
#         # host execution, so uncommenting this phase moves the project's
#         # `host_steps` (dwe test list -o json) above zero.
#         when:
#           type: shell
#           cmd: "test ! -d services/app/src/node_modules"
#         check: auto

--------
=== workspace/services/app/service.yml ===
# workspace/services/app/service.yml — the "app" starter service.
#
# The folder name (app) is the service's map key — there is no `name:`
# field. Run `dwe docs show config/services/index` for the full schema.

type: app
container: "app"

# Source hub: `dir` is the host directory holding this app's checkout (created
# by the deploy pipeline, gitignored), mounted at `dir_internal` inside the
# container. Mount the whole hub, not just the sources — build artefacts,
# caches and tooling state live next to `src/`. `work_dir_internal` is where
# `dwe cmd` / bridged commands run.
dir: "./services/app"
dir_internal: /workspace
work_dir_internal: /workspace/src

icon: "📦"

info:
  title: "app"

# required: true              # always-on; removes the enable/disable toggle
# depends_on: []

# Ports are DISPLAY-ONLY on their own: `dwe status` and info blocks read them,
# but nothing binds them. To bind one, uncomment the pair — the port here AND
# the matching `exports.env` rule in workspace/defaults.yml that turns it into
# an environment variable your compose.yaml can reference.
# ports:
#   http: 8080

# hosts:
#   web: "app.localhost"

=== workspace/templates/ai/default/AGENTS.md.tmpl ===
# {{ .Resolved }} — source hub of the {{ .Project.Name }} DWE project

This directory is the **hub** of the `{{ .Resolved }}` service: the checkout plus
everything that lives next to it (build artefacts, caches, tooling state). It is
mounted into the container at `{{ .ServiceCfg.DirInternal }}`; commands run in
`{{ .ServiceCfg.WorkDirInternal }}`.

The environment around it is managed by the `dwe` CLI from the **project root**
(the parent of `services/`). Run `dwe` commands there, not here.

## Orientation

```
dwe docs llms-txt --lang en
```

Loads a project-aware index of services, commands, pipeline builtins, diagnostic
flags and docs pointers. Read it once, then navigate on demand.

## Working on this service

- `dwe commands list` — this project's declared dev commands; `dwe cmd <id>` runs one
- `dwe shell {{ .Resolved }} -c '<cmd>'` — a one-off command inside the container
- `dwe logs {{ .Resolved }}` — stream this service's logs
- `dwe status` — stack health and container names

> This file is **generated** by `dwe render ai` from
> `workspace/templates/ai/default/AGENTS.md.tmpl` in the project root. Edit the
> template, not this file. `CLAUDE.md` next to it is a symlink to this file.
>
> The project root has its own `AGENTS.md` — that one is scaffolded once and is
> meant to be edited by hand.

--------
=== workspace/templates/ai/default/manifest.yml ===
# workspace/templates/ai/default/manifest.yml — AI template pack (ACTIVE).
#
# `dwe render ai` renders this pack into each app service's HUB directory
# (services/<name>/, gitignored and absent until the first clone). `default` is
# the last link of the implicit resolution chain, so it applies to every service
# that has no pack of its own; add workspace/templates/ai/<service>/ to give one
# service a different pack.
#
# A manifest is strict-decoded and must declare at least one entry — unlike the
# pipeline mirrors, this file cannot ship commented.
#
# Schema and template variables: `dwe docs show render/ai`

render:
  - from: AGENTS.md.tmpl
    to: AGENTS.md

# The hub CLAUDE.md mirrors the hub AGENTS.md, exactly as the project root does.
symlinks:
  - link: CLAUDE.md
    to: AGENTS.md

--------
=== workspace/tests/smoke.yml ===
# workspace/tests/smoke.yml — starter integration-test scenario.
#
# `dwe test run smoke` copies the project into a disposable directory, gives the
# copy its own compose project name and freshly allocated host ports, deploys it
# from a clean slate, runs the steps below, then tears the copy down.
#
# This is the ONE scaffold file that ships ACTIVE rather than fully commented:
# the scenario loader is strict and rejects an empty document, so there is
# nothing here to uncomment.
#
# It is also deliberately free of assertions: on a fresh scaffold compose.yaml
# declares no services, so the deploy the scenario wraps fails at `start/up`
# with "empty compose file" and `dwe test run smoke` reports a failure. The
# scenario becomes meaningful once app exists in compose.yaml — then
# add steps here; an `http_check` builtin against the service's exported port is
# the usual first assertion.
#
# Schema and step reference: `dwe docs show config/tests`

description: "Smoke test: the stack deploys from a clean slate"

# timeout: 15m

# Per-scenario overrides applied to the copy only. `auto` is the one magic
# value: it allocates a free host port before the copy is deployed.
# env:
#   services:
#     enable: ["app"]
#   vars:
#     app.port: auto

steps: []
